tender.title: Provision of Insurance and Risk Related Services to Rural Stirling Housing Association Limited
tender.description: The scope of the Contract includes the provision of insurance cover, brokerage services (where applicable), professional advice, claims management and loss control services for property, legal liabilities and other general insurances as required by Rural Stirling Housing Association Limited for a period of three years commencing 01.04.2027, with the option to extend by up to a further two years at Rural Stirling Housing Association Limited’s sole discretion. Bids are invited from suitably qualified and experienced insurance brokers and direct insurers. The Contract will follow the Competitive Flexible Procedure with bidders being selected on the basis of the responses contained in the pre qualifying SPD. Bidders will be expected have the capability, capacity, financial and economic standing and experience to perform the contract. SPDs must be completed in full with all relevant information supplied. The Contract will be awarded on the basis of Most Economically Advantageous Tender, with specific evaluation criteria detailed within the Invitation To Tender and contract documents.

releases.description:
Credit Checks
1.The Council shall obtain a Creditsafe credit check and will score bidders accordingly:
71 - 100   Very Low Risk – Accept
51 - 70 Low Risk - Accept
30 - 50 Moderate Risk – subject to further discussion internally with the option to reject.
21-29 High Risk – subject to further discussion internally with the option to reject.
1-20 Very High Risk – Reject.
2. Please state current turnover (if contract value is over 50% of reported turnover, further discussion will be had internally with the option to reject).
3. If you are under no obligation to publish accounts on Companies House and/or do not have a comprehensive credit rating then provide audited financial accounts for the previous two years. Both quick and current ratios should be a minimum of 1:1.5 for the two successive years.  Bidders whose ratios do not meet the minimum criteria will be rejected. Bidders who can provide audited accounts but chose not to do so shall be rejected.
4. Bidders who have been trading for less than one year and cannot provide audited accounts must submit the cash flow for the current year and a letter from the bank outlining the current cash and credit position for the current year and subsequent year. This will be subject to internal discussion with the option to reject.
5. If bidder still does not meet the financial criteria for consideration but has a parent company that does, the firm may still be eligible for consideration where their submission is supported by a parent company guarantee.
Insurance
It is a requirement of this contract that bidders hold, or can commit to obtain prior to the commencement of any subsequently awarded contract, the types and levels of insurance indicated below:
Employer’s Liability Insurance = GBP10m
Public Liability Insurance = GBP5m

tender.title: 2026 - Aberdeen City - Integrated Children with Disabilities Services
tender.description: Aberdeen City Council requires the provision of an integrated specialist support service for disabled children and young people aged from birth to 18 years who have complex and/or significant care and support needs requiring a level of specialist support beyond that ordinarily available through universal, community-based or mainstream care provision. This may include children and young people with complex health, physical, learning, developmental, sensory, communication and/or behavioural support needs, including needs associated with autism. Eligibility for, and the nature of, support will be determined by individual assessment of need, intended outcomes and the Service Provider's ability to meet those needs safely and appropriately. Short-break overnights and residential care will in the main be utilised for our older children (often teenagers.)

lots.description:
The integrated support model will consist of the following elements:
1.Home and Community Outreach
Tailored, person centred support for children and their families via a combination of:
-Outreach support
-Care at home
-Whole-family support
2.Residential Care
Specialist residential care for up to four children who are no longer able to remain living at home.   As noted above, residential provision will in the main be utilised for older children, often teenagers.)
3.Residential Overnight and Short-Break Services
High-quality, child-centred residential and short-break services. Residential short breaks will in the main be utilised for our older children (often teenagers) in line with their age and stage of development.
The Services will be delivered through a hub-and-spoke model centred on the Service Provider’s properties in Aberdeen. The Service Provider will establish and maintain effective working relationships with Aberdeen City Council’s Social Work Service, community-based services, Orchard Brae School, other schools, health services, and relevant partner organisations. Additional information: The annual funding for Year 1 of the contract will be GBP2295000.  Funding for the initial 3 year term is estimated at GBP6885000 with an estimated total maximum expenditure of over the over the full five-year contract term including both optional extensions of GBP11475000.

otherRequirements.reductionCriteria:
PCS-T Question 4A.2 - Care Inspectorate Registration
Bidders must confirm that they are appropriately registered with the Care Inspectorate for the services required.
PCS-T Question 4C.1.2 – Relevant Experience
Bidders will be required to provide examples that demonstrate that they have the relevant experience to deliver the services as described. A minimum of two examples will be required. Examples of relevant experience are delivering residential care or buildings based respite care to Children and young people aged from birth to 18 years with physical disabilities, complex health needs and/or autism.

tender.title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?

classification.description: Research and development services and related consultancy services

tender.description:
Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities.
While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred.
This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenants’ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources.
Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.
